figures.caption: The antibacterial activity of five predicted potential AMPs. a, c Bacterial colonies in a Petri dish of 0.01 M pH7.4 PBS (a, negative control), kanamycin (b, positive control), peptide L1 (c), peptide L2 (d), peptide L8 (e), peptide L10 (f) and peptide L12 (g) with V. alginolyticus and S. pyogenes, respectively. b, d Antimicrobial activity of samples in a and c, respectively. e Bacterial colonies in a Petri dish of 0.01 M pH 7.4 PBS (a, c, e, g, i, k and m) or peptide L1 (b, d, f, h, j, l and n) with V. parahaemolyticus (a, b), V. fluvialis (c, d), V. alginolyticus (e, f), E. coli (g, h), A. hydrophila (i, j), S. aureus (k, l) and S. pyogenes (m, n), respectively. f Antimicrobial activity of samples in e. The concentration of the five peptides and kanamycin is 0.5 mg/ml. The experiments were carried out in triplicate, repeated at least three times and the significant difference was determined by one-way ANOVA relative to control and indicated by asterisks (*p < 0.05, **p < 0.01 and ***p < 0.001). Data are presented as mean ± SD. Error bars represent standard deviation (SD) for the three independent experiments
